Subject: Re: AcmeBank  region pinning, backups and data residency follow-up

Hi Ryan / Sofia

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: Ensure all customer data for AcmeBank production traffic is pinned to US regions with documented failover behavior for cross-region incidents.
- Open questions we committed to follow up on:
  1) Exact definition of PII types you need treated as resident in-region (example list in attachment).
  2) Backup retention windows and whether encrypted backups may be stored outside the US for disaster recovery.
  3) Audit/logging detail required (full request/response bodies vs metadata-only).

Next steps:
- We attached a short design doc that outlines region-pinning options (single-region pinning, active-active with in-region keying, and active-primary w/ cross-region cold backups). Marissa will add the recommended configuration and expected RPO/RTO per option.
- Vanessa will share SOC2 and inventory artifacts around where logs are stored and how long they're retained.
- Can we lock a follow-up on Friday 4/20 at 10am PT to review the design and confirm the preferred backup approach?

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-design.pdf (high-level options)

Ring any clarifying questions. I left a few presumed decisions in the doc but can change based on what you need.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: AcmeBank  region pinning, backups and data residency follow-up

Aditya

Thanks for the summary and the design doc. A couple of clarifications from our side before the Friday call: 

1) PII scope: We need the following to remain resident in the US at all times: full name, SSN, DOB, account numbers, and any customer-uploaded documents that contain the above. Metadata (timestamps, request IDs) can be stored outside the US if encrypted, but we prefer storing logs in-region if possible.

2) Backups: Our security team allows encrypted backups outside the US only if the encryption keys are customer-managed (HSM) and the backups are limited to cold storage with a longer restore SLA (we expect documented RPO/RTO).

3) Failover: Prefer an active-primary model with cross-region read replicas for non-PII to reduce latency, but primary write region must enforce region pinning for PII. We'd like to understand how Redwood handles KV cache and KV evictions when pinning is enforced.

I attached a short note from our compliance team (see inline below). Also please share SOC2 summary and any relevant audit log retention defaults you have. Friday 10am PT works for us.

Ryan
Director, Cloud Security, AcmeBank
ryan.miller@acmebank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: AcmeBank  region pinning, backups and data residency follow-up

Hi Ryan, thanks for the details, very helpful. Quick technical clarifications and where they map to our design doc: 

- PII handling: We can enforce region pinning at the customer routing layer so that any request tagged for AcmeBank (tenant ID header) will only be routed to US-serving inference clusters. For attachments / uploaded documents we support policy-level blocking of cross-region replication.

- KV cache and eviction: KV cache is sharded by serving cluster; when region pinning is enabled we keep KV shards and cache stores inside the pinned region. Eviction behaves as normal LRU; cache misses will fetch from the model weights and KV store in-region. This will increase cold start token latency for cross-region requests but preserves residency guarantees.

- Backups and keys: We support encrypted, customer-managed key (KMS/HSM) for backups. If you prefer off-US cold backups, we can configure them to only be restorable with your HSM key (never accessible by Redwood without your key). We'll include the expected RPO/RTO options in the updated doc.

- Logs & audit: Default platform retention for verbose request logs is 90 days; we can extend per-contract. We can also provide metadata-only logs for export outside the US while keeping full request bodies resident (either in our US logging cluster or in your VPC when on Private deployment).

I've updated the design doc with a recommended config (Option B  - US primary, cold encrypted backups in EU with customer-managed keys, pre-approved failover procedure). See attached: redwood-region-pinning-design.pdf (page 4).

Attachments: soc2-summary.pdf; backup-failover-playbook.xlsx

Regards,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Couple of practical notes from ops/security side: 

- Canary failover: We recommend a staged failover test using a canary tenant to validate the KV eviction behavior and cold-start latency hit before executing for production. We can run this in our US staging and provide telemetry.

- Monitoring: We'll export per-tenant telemetry to the shared console and can create a read-only view for your SREs. Trail of changes (who initiated failover, timestamp, metrics) is captured in our audit logs.

- Paperwork: I'll drop the SOC2 summary and the backup playbook into the Drive folder (link below) and send a DocuSign for the small addendum about customer-managed keys.

Vanessa

2) Please surface the exact audit log fields we will get for 1-year retention and how redaction works for request bodies.
